items.followUp: What are derived quantities and derived units?

accept: not defined in terms of other quantities
rubric.why: Checks the definition of base quantities.
rubric.description: Defines base quantities as independent quantities that are not defined in terms of other quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

accept: units used to measure base quantities
rubric.why: Checks the definition of base units.
rubric.description: Defines base units as the units used to measure base quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

modelAnswer: Base quantities are independent quantities that are not defined in terms of other quantities.
Base units are the units used to measure base quantities.

items.followUp: Define impulse and write its formula.

accept: product of the mass and velocity
rubric.description: Defines momentum as the product of a body's mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.
Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass and velocity of a body.
Formula: p = mv, where p is momentum, m is mass and v is velocity.

items.followUp: State the first condition of equilibrium and write its formula.

accept: sum of clockwise moments equals sum of anticlockwise moments
rubric.why: Checks the statement of the second condition of equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments, so the resultant torque is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct condition.

accept: sum of clockwise moments=sum of anticlockwise moments
rubric.why: Checks the formula for the second condition of equilibrium.
rubric.description: Writes the equilibrium relation that the net torque is zero, or that clockwise and anticlockwise moments are equal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

modelAnswer: The second condition of equilibrium is that the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.
Formula: Στ = 0, or sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments.
